Rupali Bank Limited ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat Chittagong and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: Zinat Ara J : In this Rule Nisi, the petitioner has challenged the legality of order No. 143 dated 22-2-2011 passed by respondent No. 1. the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Artha Jari Case No. 1916 of 2003 (Annexure-K to the writ petition), releasing the mortgaged properties from the Artha Jari Case violating the provision of section 31 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Petitioner-Rupali Bank Limited (shortly, the Bank) is a banking company constituted under the Companies Act. Respondent No. 10, M/s. Zaman Rahman Limited (hereinafter stated as the Company) is a loanee company. The Company availed various loan facilities from the Bank including Overdraft, Cash Credit (Hypothecation), Packing Credit, L/C facilities, etc. The loan limits of the Company were enhanced from time to time and it stood at Tk. 3,00,00,000 on 5-8-1986. The Company also availed Overdraft facilities of Taka 11,80,413.88 from the Bank. As a security for repayment of loans, the Company mortgaged lands measuring 10 Gonda + 2.43 acres fully and effectually described in schedules-Ka, Kha and Ga of the plaint of the Artha Rin Suit. A deed of mortgage was executed by the Company in favour of the Bank being mortgaged deed No. 5202 dated 4-8-1986. The Company had purchased Kha and Ga scheduled 2.43 acres of land, as fully described in the schedules of the plaint of the Artha Rin Suit as well as Execution Case, from the seller Abdus Salam Chowdhury by seven registered deeds being Nos. 11089 dated 29-9-1977, 11231 dated 3-10-1977, 11071 dated 28-9-1977, 11127 dated 30-9-1977, 11138 dated 30-9-1977, 11108 dated 29-9-1977 and 11188 dated 1-10-1977. As consideration of the aforesaid properties/lands, the Company allotted 126 shares in favour of seller Abdus Salam Chowdhury and also appointed him as a director of the Company in its meeting dated 25-8-1977. The Company having failed to repay the loan, the Bank, as plaintiff, on 12.05.1988, filed Mortgage Suit No. 79 of 1988 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Commercial Court, Chittagong, for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 3,17,07,681.83 including interest as stood on 31-3-1988 impleading the Company, its Managing Director-Akhtaruzzaman, Zinat Ara Begum and AHM Mokhlesur Rahman as defendants of the suit. The suit was decreed on 24-4-1989 in preliminary form. The preliminary decree was made final on 14-6-1989. Thereafter, the Bank, on 25-3-1992, filed Mortgaged Execution Case No. 07 of 1992 before the said Court for recovery of Taka 5,77,83,747.83 including interest. Subsequently, Mortgage Execution Case was converted into Artha Jan Case No. 1916 of 2003 of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong (the Adalat, in brief) after promulgation of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the Ain). The Bank, with the permission of the Adalat, purchased the decretal property mentioned in schedule-Ka of the plaint of the suit at Taka 30,00,000 and the said amount was adjusted with the decretal dues. Thereafter, the sale was confirmed by the Adalat in favour of the decree-holder-Bank. But the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong, by order dated 29-3-2009, inadvertently disposed of the said Artha Jari Case with full satisfaction. The Bank then filed an application before the Adalat, on 28-6-2009, to restore the Artha Jail Case. The learned Judge of the Adalat, by order dated 28-6-2009, allowed the said application and restored the Artha Jari Case to its original file and number. Thereafter, the Bank, on 13-7-2009, filed an application before the Adalat for amending the execution petition by incorporating the decretal amount of Taka 30,32,49,690 including interest as stood on 30-6-2009 under the decree. Eventually, the Bank got possession of the Ka scheduled property through Adalat on 25-9-2008. Meanwhile, the borrower in the name of another company, namely, M/s. Texan Products Limited (shortly, Texan), filed Other Class Suit No. 07 of 1996 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong challenging the judgment and decree passed in favour the Bank in Mortgage Suit No. 79 of 1988 and the proceeding of Mortgage Execution Case No. 07 of 1992 arising out of the said suit. On an application filed by the Bank under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of the suit, the learned Judge of the said Court, by judgment and order dated 17-8-1098, rejected the plaint of the suit. Thereafter, Texan filed First Appeal No. 14 of 1999 before the High Court Division. In the said appeal, an order of injunction was passed vide Civil Rule No. 53(F) of 1999. Eventually, Civil Rule No. 53(F) of 1999 was discharged on 16-7-2006 by the High Court Division and the order of injunction was vacated. First Appeal No. 14 of 1999 was also dismissed on 22-4-2010 by the High Court Division. Prior to that one Abdus Salam Chowdhury, predecessor of respondent’s No. 2 to 9, on 22-1-1987, had filed Title Suit No. 08 of 1987 before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against the borrower Company for cancellation of seven registered deeds and recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 8-12-1987. In the said suit, the Bank was not made a party, although the properties were mortgaged in favour of the Bank. The Bank, after knowing about the said collusive decree obtained from the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong in Title Suit No. 08 of 1997, on 11.09.1988, had filed Other Suit No. 47 of 1988 against Abdus Salam Chowdhury and the loanee Company for declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 08.12:1997 'passed in Other Suit No. 08 of 1987 is fraudulent, collusive, void, etc. During pendency of the suit, Abdus Salam Chowdhury had died and his heirs were substituted as defendants No. 1(Ka) to 1(Ja) in the suit and they contested the suit, but the suit was, eventually, decreed in favour of the Bank on 31-3- 2002. Respondents No. 2 to 9, successors of Abdus Salam Chowdhury, then filed Other Appeal No. 526 of 2002 before the District Judge, Chittagong and the said appeal is still pending for hearing. On 10-1-2011, respondent’s No. 2 to 9 filed an application in the Execution Case for excluding Schedules-Kha and Ga mortgaged properties from the schedule of the Execution Case claiming ownership to the said properties. The Bank filed specific objection against it on the ground of maintainability of the Execution Case inasmuch as the third-party-claimant-respondents No. 2 to 9 had not complied with the provision of section 32 of the Ain, but the learned Judge of the Adalat, without considering the fact that Schedule-Ka and Ga properties were mortgaged in favour of the Bank and that respondents No. 2 to 9 have not complied with the provision of section 32 of the Ain, unlawfully released those properties.
